blurb: One of the smallest terriers, with a long silky steel-blue and tan coat
description: The Yorkshire Terrier is a British toy terrier from Yorkshire, weighing up to 3.2 kg, with a long silky blue-grey and tan coat and a playful nature.
answer: The Yorkshire Terrier, or Yorkie, is a British toy terrier that originated in nineteenth-century Yorkshire and is among the smallest of all dog breeds, weighing no more than 3.2 kg. Its long, fine, silky coat is dark steel-grey on the body and tan on the head, and it is described as playful and energetic.

body: Workers from Scotland brought several kinds of terrier to Yorkshire in the mid-nineteenth century, and mill and mine workers bred them into a small ratting terrier, possibly using the Paisley and Clydesdale Terriers. The show dog Huddersfield Ben, owned by Mary Ann Foster in the late 1860s, defined the breed type and is still called the father of the breed. The Yorkie reached North America in 1872 and was first registered with the AKC in 1885. It contributed to the Silky Terrier and the Biewer Terrier.

The Kennel Club calls for a glossy, fine, straight and silky coat, traditionally grown very long and parted down the back. It is dark grey to black from the neck to the tail and a rich tan on the head, chest and legs; no other colours are accepted by the Kennel Club or the FCI. Puppies are born darker, and the coat can take three years or more to reach its final colour.
The Yorkshire Terrier is described as playful and energetic and is usually kept as a companion. The Kennel Club describes its ideal carriage as very upright, conveying an important air.

The traditional long coat is very high maintenance and can knot without daily brushing, so many owners keep it trimmed short. Yorkies shed relatively little. Because of their small size they are easily injured by falls, other dogs or clumsy handling, and many veterinarians recommend a harness rather than a collar for walks.

Conditions reported in the breed include portosystemic shunt, tracheal collapse, luxating patella, Legg–Calvé–Perthes disease, periodontal disease, cataracts, dry eye, distichiasis, colour dilution alopecia and hypoglycaemia in small puppies. The breed has an above-average life expectancy; a 2024 UK study found 13.3 years.

faq.q: How big does a Yorkshire Terrier get?
faq.a: Yorkies are among the smallest dog breeds, with a standard weight of no more than 3.2 kg.
Yorkies shed less than many breeds, losing small amounts when bathed or brushed, but the long coat needs regular brushing.

faq.q: How long do Yorkshire Terriers live?
faq.a: The breed has an above-average life expectancy; UK studies have found about 12.5 to 13.3 years.

faq.q: Is the Yorkshire Terrier recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 86 in Group 3, terriers.
